title: Fires & Tunnel Emergencies
whatItIs: If your vehicle catches fire, get everyone out to a safe place and call the fire brigade. Don't open a burning engine compartment. In tunnels, keep your distance.
keyFacts: Don't try to put out an engine compartment fire: opening it will make the fire flare.
Smell burning rubber, petrol or an electrical fault? Investigate immediately: do not risk a fire.
Never smoke or use a mobile phone on a fuel station forecourt: both are major fire risks.
Large vehicle in a tunnel: allow a four-second gap. If you stop, leave at least 5 metres.
Signs in road tunnels show the direction and distance to an emergency exit.

items.title: Stop safely
items.text: If you can, stop in a place of relative safety. Hazard lights on.

items.title: Get everyone out
items.text: Get the occupants out quickly and to a safe place.

items.title: Keep it shut
items.text: Don't open the engine compartment: the fire will flare.

items.title: Call 999
items.text: Ask for the fire brigade. Give the exact location and direction of travel.

a.label: Engine fire
points: Get everyone out and call the fire brigade

b.label: Overheated engine
points: Wait until it has cooled naturally
Only then remove the coolant cap

onTheTest.question: Smoke is coming from your lorry's engine compartment. What should you do?
options: Get out and call the fire brigade without opening it
Open it to find the fire
Drive on to the next services
onTheTest.why: Get the occupants out quickly to a safe place and call the fire brigade. Opening the engine compartment will make the fire flare.

onTheTest.question: You have to stop in a tunnel. What gap should you leave to the vehicle in front?
onTheTest.why: If you have to stop in a tunnel, leave at least a 5-metre gap. A four-second gap is for a large vehicle moving through a tunnel.

traps: Moving in a tunnel: four seconds. Stopped in a tunnel: at least 5 metres.
Fire and further collisions are the main dangers after a crash: switch engines off.
Spilt diesel makes the road very slippery: don't overfill, and check the fuel cap seals.
